title: Bolivia's Sky Mirror: a $70 Tour. China's Chaka: ¥60 at the Gate | China Travel Expert
description:
Bolivia's Salar de Uyuni — the salt flat that turns into a mirror of the sky — costs a $60–80 guided day tour to reach. China has its own sky mirror, and you walk onto it for ¥60.

Uyuni is the bucket-list "mirror of the sky," but it's remote: you reach it on a guided tour, and 1-day mirror tours run about $60–80 (multi-day trips start around $290). China's version is Chaka Salt Lake in Qinghai — the same optical trick of still, shallow water over a salt-white bed reflecting the sky. Entry is ¥60 in peak season (about eight US dollars), and a bullet train from Xining gets you there in roughly an hour for ¥34. Chaka sits at 3,059 metres, and the mirror effect is strongest on a calm, clear day after rain. Honest caveat: the Uyuni price is a full guided tour (driver, lunch, remote logistics), while ¥60 is just Chaka's gate — but the gap on simply standing on the mirror is real, roughly eight to one.

🧭 Expert Tip: for the cleanest reflection at Chaka, go on a windless morning right after rain, and wear the shoe covers sold at the gate — the brine is rough on shoes.
